panels.title: Pressure Stall (PSI)
panels.description: Watch: sustained plateaus, not spikes. OK: cpu/io < 5%, memory ≈ 0. Fix: grow infra(?)

panels.title: CPU Usage
panels.description: Watch: user/system/iowait and the steal line. OK: headroom below 100%, steal < 2–5%. Fix: user = Top Queries by CPU; system = use / configure properly a pooler; steal = hypervisor

panels.title: Load Average
panels.description: Watch: load1 vs the cores line. OK: load < cores. Fix: with low CPU% — processes queue on disk -> disk panels; with high CPU% -> CPU Usage

panels.title: Memory Available
panels.description: Watch: trend (MemAvailable = free + reclaimable cache; shared_buffers and hugepages excluded). OK: > 15–20%. Fix: pooler / lower work_mem * connections, add RAM; cross-check PSI memory — available can lie, PSI does not.

panels.title: Disk Latency
panels.description: Watch: per device, the WAL volume separately. OK: SSD/NVMe single-digit ms, > 10–20 ms is bad. Fix: growth at unchanged IOPS — disk dm-* (LVM) volumes are shown alongside their physical disks — per-device lines, nothing is double-counted.

panels.title: Disk IOPS
panels.description: Watch: proximity to the volume limit, sawtooth in checkpoint rhythm. OK: < ~70% of the limit. Fix: find the consumer (pg_stat_io, tops), make longer checkpoints, raise volume class/size dm-* (LVM) volumes are shown alongside their physical disks — per-device lines, nothing is double-counted.

panels.title: Disk Throughput
panels.description: Volume bandwidth: sequential scans, backups and replication eat MB/s at modest IOPS — this catches what Disk IOPS misses. Compare with pg_stat_io reads/writes ×8192 (Instance: IO Attribution) to see whose bytes these are. OK: below the volume's rated throughput. Fix: find the eater (pg_stat_io → query tops), move backups off-hours, faster volume. dm-* (LVM) volumes are shown alongside their physical disks — per-device lines, nothing is double-counted.

panels.title: Disk Space Free
panels.description: Watch: worst volume trend — WAL/temp can eat space rapidly. OK: > 20–25%. Fix: WAL Directory Size (slot? archiver?) -> temp spills (Top Queries by Temp) -> bloat (pg_repack)

panels.title: Disk Queue Depth
panels.description: Watch: aqu-sz growth — it leads latency growth. OK: SATA/SAS SSD single digits, NVMe tens. Fix: as Disk Latency — find and spread the load, or a faster disk dm-* (LVM) volumes are shown alongside their physical disks — per-device lines, nothing is double-counted.

panels.title: Swap I/O
panels.description: Watch: sustained swap-out (swap-in is just reading back). OK: 0. Fix: memory shortage — see Memory Available and PSI; vm.swappiness 1–10

panels.title: Swap / Dirty Memory
panels.description: Watch: dirty growth on a slow disk = incoming writeback storm; used swap never shrinks by itself. OK: dirty well below vm.dirty_bytes. Fix: lower vm.dirty_*_bytes, faster disk, spread checkpoints

panels.title: OOM Kills
panels.description: Watch: any value > 0. OK: strictly 0 — an OOM-killed backend = crash-recovery of the whole instance. Fix: victim in dmesg; vm.overcommit_memory=2

panels.title: Network Traffic
panels.description: Watch: NIC ceiling; spikes = replication/backups. OK: < ~70% of bandwidth. Fix: move backups/replication in time or to another interface; faster NIC

panels.title: Network Errors
panels.description: Watch: any sustained non-zero rate. OK: 0. Fix: driver/cable/MTU/ring buffers (ethtool) — infrastructure

panels.title: Transactions
panels.description: Watch: a commit dip while waits grow = queued; rollback growth = errors/deadlocks/retries. Fix: DB Load (AAS) → by wait class.

panels.title: Connections
panels.description: Watch: client backends vs max_connections. OK: < 80%. Fix: pooler; who took the slots — Connections by Role.

panels.title: Connections by Role
panels.description: Watch: which database/role ate the max_connections slots. Fix: pooler for the culprit, per-role connection limit.

panels.title: Sessions by State
panels.description: Watch: idle growth — an app without a pooler; idle in transaction growth — a source of locks and bloat. OK: idle in tx ≈ 0. Fix: pooler; idle_in_transaction_session_timeout.

panels.title: Checkpoints
panels.description: Watch: requested checkpoints appearing. OK: timed only. Fix: raise max_wal_size; who generates WAL — Top Queries by WAL.

panels.title: WAL Generation
panels.description: Watch: bytes/s, buffers_full, FPI share right after a checkpoint. Fix: buffers_full growing → raise wal_buffers; high FPI → wal_compression / less frequent checkpoints; culprit — Top Queries by WAL.

panels.title: WAL Latency
panels.description: Watch: ms/op — the main commit latency driver under sync replication. OK: fsync single-digit ms. Fix: the disk under WAL (Disk Latency, OS), separate volume, synchronous_commit.

panels.title: Disk Writes by Backend
panels.description: Watch: who dominates — checkpointer/bgwriter/autovacuum/client. Fix: per culprit: spread checkpoints, vacuum cost, queries (Workload).

panels.title: Disk Reads by Backend
panels.description: Watch: client reads growing = the working set no longer fits in memory. Fix: RAM/shared_buffers; who reads — Top Queries by Buffer Misses / Disk Reads.

panels.title: Cache Hit Ratio
panels.description: Watch: a sustained DOWNWARD trend, not the level. OK: > 99% for OLTP. Fix: RAM/shared_buffers; percentages deceive — cross-check absolute Disk Reads by Backend.

panels.title: I/O Time by Backend
panels.description: Watch: seconds of IO per second per subsystem (can exceed 1 — parallelism). Fix: by the dominating subsystem — checkpoints/vacuum/queries.

panels.title: I/O Latency (pg_stat_io)
panels.description: Watch: ms/op vs Disk Latency (OS): matches — disk-bound; much lower — the page cache is saving you. Fix: as Disk Latency.

panels.title: Buffer Evictions & Bgwriter
panels.description: Watch: evictions = pressure on shared_buffers; maxwritten_clean = bgwriter hitting its limit. Fix: raise shared_buffers, raise bgwriter_lru_maxpages.

panels.title: Checkpoint & Block I/O Time
panels.description: Watch: checkpoint write/sync busy share and per-DB block IO time (can exceed 1). Fix: spread checkpoints; detailed attribution — I/O Time by Backend.

panels.title: PostgreSQL Up
panels.description: When the DB is down the pg_up series DISAPPEARS. Fix: exporter/network/database — collection health is up{job=~"sql-.*"}

panels.title: Uptime
panels.description: Watch: a sharp drop = restart/crash-recovery/failover (red — younger than 10 min). Fix: reason in PG logs; cross-check OOM Kills

panels.title: WAL Directory Size
panels.description: Watch: pg_wal vs the max_wal_size reference — checkpoints alone keep it near max_wal_size; growth beyond it = a dead slot or stuck archiver is holding WAL and checkpoints cannot free it. Fix: dead slot (Replication Slots), stuck archiver (WAL Archiver), checkpoints not keeping up

panels.title: WAL Archiver
panels.description: Watch: the .ready queue and last-success age — failed==0 with a STUCK archiver is false calm. OK: queue ≈ 0. Fix: archive_command/storage; a growing queue will fill the disk.

panels.title: Locks
panels.description: Watch: the waiting series (granted=false) — the lock queue. OK: steadily 0 waiting. Fix: who holds whom — Blocking Sessions (Workload).

panels.title: Deadlocks & Temp Files
panels.description: Watch: deadlocks/min > 0; temp bytes/s. Fix: deadlock — lock acquisition order in the app; temp — work_mem / the plan (Top Queries by Temp).

panels.title: Session Errors
panels.description: Watch: any sustained fatal/killed rate. OK: 0. Fix: killed — find who kills (OOM? admin?); fatal — client-side errors and auth failures. Page corruption lives in Checksum Failures.

panels.title: Checksum Failures
panels.description: Cumulative on purpose: a rate would erase the incident from the panel minutes after it happened. OK: 0 failures AND checksums enabled — with data_checksums off the zero means nothing is being verified, not that pages are healthy. Fix: any growth = page corruption; restore the relation from backup/replica and check disk/RAM. Enabling needs initdb --data-checksums or offline pg_checksums.

panels.title: Config Errors
panels.description: Broken lines in pg_hba.conf (hba) / postgresql.conf (config): a reload does NOT apply them — the server silently keeps the OLD values, and the NEXT restart will fail on them. OK: both 0. Fix: the exact lines are in pg_hba_file_rules / pg_file_settings (WHERE error IS NOT NULL); restart-pending changes are a different signal (pending restart line in Long Transactions & 2PC).

panels.title: Long Transactions & 2PC
panels.description: Watch: transactions holding vacuum and xmin; forgotten prepared xacts. OK: prepared ≈ 0. Fix: kill/fix the client; COMMIT/ROLLBACK PREPARED; apply pending restarts in a window.

panels.title: SLRU Caches
panels.description: Watch: read/written spikes on SubtransSLRU/MultiXact — sudden degradation, visible in AAS only as an anonymous LWLock. Fix: long transactions with savepoints, SELECT FOR SHARE; PG17 — SLRU size GUCs.

panels.title: Transaction ID Age
panels.description: Watch: growth without a plateau = autovacuum can't freeze fast enough; the only metric able to stop the database entirely. OK: well below 200M. Fix: Xmin Horizon (who holds it), workers/cost limit.

panels.title: Vacuum Progress
panels.description: Watch: a phase stuck for hours = a huge table or a throttled cost limit. Fix: raise vacuum_cost_limit / lower cost_delay; partitioning.

panels.title: Queries per Second
panels.description: Watch: a break vs baseline. Fix: growth with latency → tops; concentration — Top Queries by Calls.

panels.title: Query Latency (avg)
panels.description: Watch: the trend; the average hides tails — see Mean Latency Spread Across Queries. Fix: DB Load (AAS) → class → tops.

panels.title: Oldest Transaction / Query
panels.description: Watch: the oldest transaction holds vacuum; idle-in-tx holds locks. OK: seconds. Fix: idle_in_transaction_session_timeout, statement_timeout, fix the client.

panels.title: DB Load (AAS)
panels.description: Watch: total height vs cores and the dominating class; a Lock-class plateau of height N = N sessions queued. OK: AAS < cores. Fix: Lock → Blocking Sessions; IO → Disk Reads/Writes by Backend + tops; CPU → Top Queries by CPU.

panels.title: Blocking Sessions (live — ignores dashboard time range)

targets.rawSql:
SELECT
  w.pid                                                   AS waiter_pid,
  bp.pid                                                  AS blocker_pid,
  w.usename                                               AS waiter_user,
  b.usename                                               AS blocker_user,
  b.state                                                 AS blocker_state,
  ROUND(EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (now() - w.state_change)))::int AS wait_s,
  COALESCE(w.query_id::text, '')                          AS waiter_queryid,
  LEFT(regexp_replace(w.query, '\s+', ' ', 'g'), 70)      AS waiter_query,
  LEFT(regexp_replace(b.query, '\s+', ' ', 'g'), 70)      AS blocker_last_query
FROM pg_stat_activity w
CROSS JOIN LATERAL unnest(pg_blocking_pids(w.pid)) AS bp(pid)
JOIN pg_stat_activity b ON b.pid = bp.pid
WHERE w.wait_event_type = 'Lock'
ORDER BY wait_s DESC
LIMIT 20

panels.description: Empty = no lock queue. blocker_state = idle in transaction — the classic root cause. Live SQL as role monitoring (timeouts 5s/1s); the datasource follows the instance selector (uid pg-${node}; on «datasource not found» revert to $pgds). Fix: terminate the blocker, fix the client.

panels.title: Top Wait Events
panels.description: Watch: the specific event — DataFileRead vs WALSync vs Lock:transactionid are different diseases of one class. Fix: per event.

panels.title: Autovacuum Workers
panels.description: Watch: a plateau at the ceiling = saturation. Fix: raise autovacuum_max_workers/cost_limit.

panels.title: Xmin Horizon by Holder
panels.description: Vacuum cannot clean rows newer than the oldest xmin — this panel names WHO holds it. Sources: session (open transaction), walsender (standby with hot_standby_feedback), prepared_xact (forgotten 2PC), replication_slot (xmin/catalog_xmin, incl. a dead logical consumer). Watch: the effective horizon is the max across sources; growth = dead rows pile up cluster-wide. Fix: per source — kill/fix the session, COMMIT/ROLLBACK PREPARED, revive or drop the slot, reconsider hot_standby_feedback. Per-pid detail: activity/xmin_horizon.sql.

panels.title: Node Roles
panels.description: Cluster-wide (ignores node/host selectors): split brain is only visible with ALL nodes on one panel. 0 = primary, 1 = standby, per node. Role is state, not a label: a failover flips the line instead of renaming series. Watch: a line crossing = promote happened; two lines at 0 = split brain, no line at 0 = no primary (writes are down).

panels.title: Timeline ID
panels.description: Cluster-wide (ignores node/host selectors): timeline divergence is only visible with ALL nodes on one panel. Timeline increments on every promote — proof a failover actually happened (annotated on all panels). Watch: nodes on DIFFERENT timelines = the standby did not follow the new primary; it needs pg_rewind or a rebuild.

panels.title: Replication Lag (seconds)
panels.description: Watch: which stage lags. OK: for sync — milliseconds. Fix: write/flush — standby disk; replay — conflicts / single-threaded replay.

panels.title: Replication Lag (bytes)
panels.description: Watch: sent lag = network/walsender can't ship. Fix: network, standby disk.

panels.title: Sync Standbys
panels.description: Cluster-wide: reads whichever node is currently primary, regardless of the node selector. OK: equals the count in synchronous_standby_names. Fix: 0 = COMMITS ARE STUCK — restore standby/network now or drop sync temporarily; «no primary» = no node reports primary role (both in recovery, or exporter down — check pg-monitoring).

panels.title: WAL Receiver
panels.description: Cluster-wide: reads whichever node is currently standby, regardless of the node selector. OK: 1. Fix: 0 = the stream is broken (network/slot/timeline) — replay lag may falsely read zero meanwhile; «no standby» = no node reports standby role (promoted pair, or exporter down — check pg-monitoring).

panels.title: Replication Slots (retained WAL)
panels.description: Watch: retained WAL growing = the slot consumer is dead; safe_wal_size shrinking = headroom to slot loss. Fix: revive the consumer or DROP the slot before primary's disk fills.

panels.title: Slot Status
panels.description: Slot state as text, not a 0/1 line on a bytes axis. OK: reserved (or extended). Fix: unreserved = the slot is about to lose WAL it still needs; lost = it already did and the consumer must be rebuilt. Retained bytes and headroom — in Replication Slots (retained WAL).

panels.title: Standby Replay
panels.description: Watch: gap bytes (received, not replayed) growing = replay is the bottleneck (single process/conflicts/disk); delay seconds while primary is idle is normal. Fix: conflicts (Recovery Conflicts), standby disk.

panels.title: Recovery Conflicts
panels.description: Watch: mostly snapshot/lock — standby queries cancelled by replay. Fix: hot_standby_feedback (price — bloat on primary) or max_standby_streaming_delay.

list.name: node
list.label: Нода
list.description: Идентичность НОДЫ, не роль: после failover нода остаётся собой. Роль показывают панели Node Roles / pg_role_info.

list.name: datname
list.label: База
list.description: База для панелей объектного слоя (per-database метрики). Cluster-wide панели (Database Size, Transaction ID Age) фильтром не управляются.
